correctness.rationale: At the exact model (2.4) in Kumar--Kumari, u3'=u3[-c3+w3*u2/(d3+u2)]. Compact support strictly inside the positive octant permits integration of L(log u3) against any invariant probability, giving E h(u2)=c3/w3, h(x)=x/(d3+x). Since 0<h<1, w3>c3 is necessary. The identity h(m)-h(x)=-d(x-m)/(d+m)^2+d(x-m)^2/[(d+m)^2(d+x)] yields m-u*= (d+u*)/(d+m) E[(u2-m)^2/(d+u2)] without approximations. Equality means u2 is constant mu-a.s.; invariance makes the full support invariant, so the top equation fixes u3, and the strictly increasing x->w1*x/(d1+x)/(1+f2*u3) in the middle equation fixes u1. Ergodicity then forces a single equilibrium. Nonconstant ergodic recurrence has strict defect and positive mass below and above u* by monotonicity of h; the periodic orbit's invariant measure is ergodic. The rational parameter check c3=7/10,w3=2,d3=20 gives u*=140/13. Independent exact test of a balanced two-point law with masses 37/64 at u2=5 and 27/64 at u2=25 gives mean 215/16 and defect 555/208, matching exactly; this algebraic test is not a claim of an invariant orbit. No existence of recurrence is proved.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact universal restriction on genuinely non-equilibrium recurrent dynamics of a biologically studied tritrophic system, despite parameter-dependent existence and chaos: every positive periodic orbit must cross the fixed equilibrium middle-predator level and its mean must exceed it by an explicit weighted variance. These are checkable geometric/ergodic constraints absent from the introducing equilibrium/bifurcation work, not merely a fixed-point recomputation or numerical orbit. The Jensen step is elementary, so its value lies in the coupled dynamical strictness and all-parameter recurrent-state interpretation; it does not establish new existence/stability results.
